title: Segmented backfill coordinator with resume tokens and lineage manifests
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a coordinator service to run large-scale backfills and replays for console usage analytics using segmented partitions. The coordinator must produce idempotent, resumable work units (resume tokens), emit lineage manifests for downstream consumers, and expose observability hooks for cost/latency trade-offs. Motivation: ad-hoc retries and monolithic backfill jobs have caused long-running lock contention, OOMs on workers, and poor visibility into partial progress. This design aims to make long backfills resumable, schedulable, quota-aware, and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can start a segmented backfill over a namespace and emit per-segment resume tokens
Backfill jobs are idempotent: re-running the same resume token does not double-count events
Progress checkpoints are persisted to durable store and can be used to resume within 1 minute accuracy
Lineage manifests published for each completed segment with schema version and hash
Cost-aware throttling allows operators to limit GPU/worker concurrency and target per-hour token consumption
End-to-end integration test that replays a synthetic 7-day window using coordinator and validates metrics against golden dataset
design_decisions: Use segmented ranges (time + shard id) vs raw event offsets to make retry windows small and parallelizable
Resume token = (segment_id, last_processed_offset, manifest_hash, attempted_count) to detect partial writes and enforce idempotency
Checkpoint store will be implemented on top of existing Durable KV (redwood-durable-kv) to avoid introducing new infra
Lineage manifest published to s3 + notification to eventstream with signed URL for consumers to fetch
Throttling layers: (1) coordinator-level budget tokens, (2) per-worker backoff based on latency/error rates
Trade-offs: stronger guarantees (exact-once) would require distributed transactions; we prefer idempotent writes with dedupe keys to balance complexity vs throughput
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Coordinator service scaffolding + segmented planner (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Resume token format + durable checkpointing + idempotent writer lib (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Lineage manifest producer + publisher + consumer compatibility tests (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Observability: per-segment metrics, backfill dashboard, alert rules (1 week)
Phase 5: Canary run on non-critical namespace and post-mortem (1 week)
Phase 6: Run full 90-day historical backfill with staged concurrency increase and validate outputs
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: WIP - planner prototype completed; can compute segments for arbitrary time ranges and shard counts. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/backfill-coordinator/pull/12)
2026-02-28: Checkpoint schema v1 proposed; reviewed with storage team — switched to redwood-durable-kv for strong writes.
2026-03-05: Idempotent writer lib landed (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/data-io/pull/87). Integration tests show dedupe rate <0.01% on synthetic replay.

2026-03-10: Lineage manifest proto finalized; security reviewed manifest fields and signed-url lifecycle. Observability proto added to metrics exporter. Starting canary on analytics-dev namespace with 5 segments.
test_plan: Unit tests for resume token encoding/decoding and checkpoint application
Integration test: run coordinator over synthetic 7-day dataset; validate counts vs golden set
Chaos test: kill workers mid-segment and resume using last checkpoint; ensure no duplicates
Load test: simulate 100 concurrent segments with throttling enabled and verify cluster CPU/GPU targets
Security test: ensure lineage manifest signed URLs expire and do not leak PII
notes: Prefer small segment sizes (<= 30m wall time) for faster recoverability; we will expose segment size as a planner parameter.
Operators should be able to pause/resume backfills via Console and see per-segment failure reasons.
Potential follow-up: add cost-estimate projection before starting a backfill based on historical per-token cost
